summary.text: 假 is conventionally analyzed as a phonosemantic character: 亻 is associated with a person-related meaning, and 叚 supplies a sound cue. Its senses include “false” and “borrow,” but their historical order is unresolved.

formation.text: The conventional analysis combines semantic 亻 with phonetic 叚. A competing proposal treats 人 as an addition distinguishing 假 from 叚 in Qin-period writing; the accounts do not settle how these analyses relate.

components.text: The conventional analysis assigns 亻 a person-related meaning. A proposal that 人 was added to distinguish this graph from 叚 leaves its graphic relationship to 人 unresolved here.
叚 is conventionally analyzed as 假’s phonetic component. Descriptions of 叚’s bronze forms concern that character and do not establish a graphic sequence for 假.

sound_limitation.text: The modern reading match and one reconstructed match support a comparison for particular readings; they do not show that the relationship applies to every reading of 假.

sound.text: In modern Mandarin data, both 叚 and 假 have the reading jiǎ; 叚 is also listed with xiá. This current match alone does not establish their ancient sound relationship.
In Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese notation, 叚 and 假 in the “borrow; false” reading are both reconstructed *Cə.kˤraʔ. The same dataset gives a different reconstruction for another reading of 假.

history.text: A scholarly account places 叚 in excavated pre-Qin texts and 假 in Qin-period documents. It interprets a document dated to 221 BCE as distinguishing 叚 for lending from 假 for borrowing, and proposes 人 as a differentiating addition.
Later texts are reported to mix the spellings 叚 and 假. The available account does not trace a dated sequence of graphic changes in later script styles.

An analysis of 叚’s bronze forms describes 爪, 又, and 石 as graphic elements; accounts also record uses read as “blessing,” “fault,” interrogative words, and others. These descriptions concern 叚 and do not establish an evolutionary path for 假.

uncertainties.text: The conventional analysis assigns 亻 a semantic role and 叚 a phonetic role; another proposal treats 人 as a differentiating addition. Their relationship remains unresolved.
The proposed development from “borrow” through “simulate” to “false” is disputed; the cited accounts do not establish a dated bridge between “borrow” and “false.”
A historical sound comparison is available for one reading in Baxter–Sagart’s reconstruction, but the cited evidence does not show that it applies to every reading of 假.

senses.text: 假 is glossed as “not true,” and a cited classical example uses it to mean “false” or “not so.” The example’s first occurrence is not securely dated here.

senses.period: classical text; composition and attestation dating unresolved
senses.text: A cited classical example uses 假 for borrowing a passage. The reported Qin-period distinction between 叚 for lending and 假 for borrowing is an interpretation of a dated document.

senses.period: historical and current; first attestation unresolved
senses.text: Textual examples record temporary or acting uses, and modern definitions include “vacation.” Their dates and relationship to “borrow” or “false” are not established.

limitations.text: The cited senses establish neither their relative chronology nor a continuous semantic development. In particular, the proposed path from borrowing through simulation to falsehood remains disputed.

overview.text: 假 is conventionally analyzed as combining a person-related element with 叚 as a sound cue. It means “false” and is also used for “borrow,” but the order of these meanings is unresolved.

components.text: 亻 is assigned a person-related meaning in the conventional analysis; a proposal that 人 distinguishes 假 from 叚 leaves the graphic explanation unsettled.
叚 is conventionally treated as the sound component. The modern and reconstructed comparisons shown here concern particular readings, not every use of 假.

relationships.text: In the conventional analysis of 假, 亻 contributes a person-related meaning; a competing account treats 人 as a differentiating addition.
The conventional analysis assigns 叚 the sound role. A Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction lists matching forms for 叚 and one reading of 假; this does not establish the role for every reading.
